title: Gina settings.json
description: Bundle runtime settings: locale, server engine, CORS response headers, file upload limits, and Socket.io config.

region.description: Locale and timezone settings for this bundle.

i18n.description: Runtime i18n configuration for the per-bundle message catalogs (bundle/locales/<culture>.json). All keys are read from the bundle's merged settings.

cookieName.description: Locale-persistence cookie name read by the per-request locale negotiation (honoured since 0.5.16). null disables cookie-based negotiation; absent or empty keeps "gina_culture".

devMissingKey.description: Dev-mode prefix marker for missing catalog keys (only applied when NODE_ENV_IS_DEV is "true"). null disables the marker.

fallbackChain.description: Optional override of the default catalog-lookup fallback chain (specific culture, then base language, then settings.region.culture, then GINA_CULTURE, then "en"). null uses the default.

cultures.description: Explicit culture allowlist for the user-signal negotiation steps (URL prefix, cookie, Accept-Language), honoured since 0.5.22: a non-empty array constrains matching to the listed cultures (staged rollouts). null or [] derives from the bundle's loaded catalogs. The bundle-default step (settings.region.culture) is never constrained.

auth.description: Authentication & authorization gate settings (#COMPLY1 route authorization + #MS3 machine-caller authentication). Boot config: changes need a bundle restart. Route-level gating itself is declared in routing.json (param.requireAuth / param.roles / param.policy).

requireAuthByDefault.description: Deny-by-default authorization (#COMPLY10) — STRICTLY boolean (any other type refuses to boot: a truthy string would leave every un-annotated route silently UNGATED). When true, every route in this bundle requires an authenticated session unless its routing.json param block carries "public": true. Routes already declaring requireAuth / roles / policy are unaffected, and "public" can never un-gate one of those. Recorded PER BUNDLE, so enabling it in one bundle never changes a sibling's posture in merged mode. Fail-closed default: false.

loginRoute.description: Login bounce target for unauthenticated BROWSER navigations on gated routes: a routing.json rule name (recommended), or an absolute path like "/login". null (default) disables the bounce — every unauthenticated request to a gated route gets a 401. XHR requests always get the 401, never a redirect. The bounce is always a non-cacheable 302.

machine.description: Machine-caller (service-to-service) authentication, since 0.5.25: a request presenting `Authorization: Bearer <key>` matching a configured caller passes the authz gate without a session — it satisfies param.requireAuth, its roles match route param.roles like a session user's, and route policies receive it as { name, roles, machine: true }. Session wins when both are present. A presented-but-invalid key gets a clean 401 with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`, never the login bounce.

enabled.description: Master switch — STRICTLY boolean (any other type refuses to boot). Fail-closed default: no machine caller can authenticate until this is explicitly true.

callers.description: Named machine callers: <callerName> -> { key, roles }. The caller name becomes the audit-trail actor key (records carry machine: true).

key.description: The shared secret this caller presents as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Supports ${secret:KEY} placeholders (resolved from process.env at config load) — prefer them, with long random values (32+ bytes). Compared in constant time against a boot-computed sha256 hash; the raw key is not retained after boot.

roles.description: Roles this caller holds — matched against route param.roles exactly like a session user's roles. Absent = no roles: the caller passes requireAuth-only routes, never role-gated ones (which is also how a route stays human-only: require a role no caller holds).

authenticator.description: Optional custom authenticator: names a <bundle>/authenticators/<name>.js module (the policies/<name>.js shape applied to authN) exporting a SYNCHRONOUS function (req) returning { name, roles } or null. Runs AFTER the built-in caller map (first success wins) and regardless of Bearer presence, so it can verify any sync-checkable credential — a JWT signature, an HMAC header, an x-api-key scheme. A missing, broken or async-function module refuses to boot; at request time a throw or malformed return is fail-closed unauthenticated.

audit.description: Audit trail (#COMPLY2) — a user-attributed, append-only record of "who did what to which record when", written with self.audit(action, data). DISTINCT from lib/logger: the trail has its own store and never rides the log sinks. Boot config: changes need a bundle restart, and every shape here is linted UNCONDITIONALLY (a malformed block refuses the boot even with enabled:false, because an audit trail that is quietly OFF is a failed control). Maps to PCI-DSS req 10, SOC 2 CC7.2, HIPAA §164.312(b).

enabled.description: Master switch — STRICTLY boolean (any other type refuses to boot: a truthy string like "true" would leave the trail silently OFF, which is exactly the failure this lint exists to prevent). When true the store is built and adopted at boot, so an unwritable destination refuses the boot rather than dropping records at the first request. Fail-closed default: false.

file.description: JSONL destination for the default file backend. An absolute path is used as-is; a relative path resolves against the project root, NEVER the process cwd. null (default) means <projectPath>/logs/audit-<bundle>-<env>.jsonl — the per-bundle AND per-env filename is deliberate, so two bundles or two envs never interleave writers into one file. Mutually exclusive with `store`. NOTE: pointing two bundles at the same absolute path defeats that protection and is not detectable at boot, since each bundle lints only its own settings.

store.description: Connector-backed backend: names a connectors.json entry whose .connector supplies core/connectors/<connector>/lib/audit-store.js. Mutually exclusive with `file`. No connector ships an audit-store implementation yet (backends are demand-gated, sqlite first), so setting this today is a clean boot refusal rather than a silent fallback to the file backend — the file backend is the v1 path.

actorKey.description: Which session.user property is snapshotted as the record's actor.key. Only this property plus a COPY of user.roles is stored — never the whole user object, which would leak PII into the trail. The roles copy means a later session mutation cannot retro-edit an already-written record. Machine callers (#MS3) have no session, so their caller NAME is used instead and the record is marked machine:true.

events.description: Framework auto-events — records the framework writes without an explicit self.audit() call.

authz.description: Record every route-authorization denial as an authz.denied record (outcome '401' | 'login-bounce' | '403-roles' | '403-policy' rides in meta.outcome). STRICTLY boolean — any other type refuses to boot, because a truthy non-boolean would not actually opt out. Note that unauthenticated 401s are attacker-triggerable, so this line is attacker-writable in volume, like any log line; throttling is a separate concern.

chain.description: Tamper-evidence hash chain (#COMPLY2 slice 3). When enabled, every record gains a `hash` chaining from its predecessor (HMAC-SHA256 over a canonical form of the record plus the previous hash), verified offline with `gina audit:verify`. Detects post-hoc edit, deletion, insertion or reordering by anyone without the signing key — NOT a defence against the process that writes the records, which holds the key and could forge a whole chain; stream the trail to WORM storage for that adversary. File backend only: a connector `store` is refused, because the chain needs the file store's ordered append. Every shape here is linted UNCONDITIONALLY, like the rest of the audit block.

enabled.description: Master switch for the chain — STRICTLY boolean (any other type refuses to boot: a truthy string like "true" would leave tamper-evidence silently OFF). When true a signing key is required or the boot refuses. Fail-closed default: false.

secret.description: The HMAC signing key. A literal, or a `${secret:VAR}` placeholder resolved at config load — the variable is read from the framework environment first, then `process.env`, so GINA_-prefixed names resolve too (before 0.6.3 the CLI sweep made them unresolvable). Optional here: when omitted the key is read from the GINA_AUDIT_SECRET environment variable. A key shorter than 32 characters boots with a warning. Enabling the chain with no key from either source refuses the boot.

server.description: HTTP server engine and protocol configuration.

engine.description: HTTP server engine. Defaults to "isaac" (built-in HTTP/2 server).

scheme.description: URL scheme. Use "https" for HTTP/2 (required) or "http" for HTTP/1.1 only.

requireHttps.description: Opt-in transport enforcement. When true, a bundle resolving a cleartext scheme (anything but "https") outside the local scope REFUSES to boot — pre-listen, so the cleartext port is never reachable. Inert in the local scope. Setting it together with allowInsecure is a boot-refused contradiction. Defaults to false: a cleartext bundle outside the local scope warns at boot instead.

allowInsecure.description: The operator's assertion that TLS terminates upstream (service mesh, ingress/load balancer, reverse proxy — the documented h2c topology). When true, the boot-time cleartext-transport warning outside the local scope becomes a single info line. Same vocabulary as mcp.json > server > allowInsecure. Setting it together with requireHttps is a boot-refused contradiction. Defaults to false.

allowHTTP1.description: When true, the HTTP/2 server also accepts HTTP/1.1 connections (ALPN negotiation). Defaults to true.

transientErrors.description: Opt-in rendering of transient datastore failures as 503 + Retry-After. When enabled, a connector error stamped isTransient that would render as HTTP 500 through throwError renders as 503 with a Retry-After header and a clean user-facing error message instead. Explicit non-500 statuses and permanent errors are never upgraded. A malformed block warns at boot and leaves the feature off — it never refuses a boot.

enabled.description: Master switch. Must be strictly boolean true to turn the upgrade on — any other type or value leaves it off. Defaults to false.

retryAfter.description: Delta-seconds value emitted as the Retry-After header on upgraded 503 responses. Integer between 1 and 86400; out-of-range or non-integer values are ignored with a boot warning. Defaults to 30.

message.description: User-facing text placed in the error field of upgraded 503 responses. Non-empty string; empty or non-string values are ignored with a boot warning. Defaults to the standard 503 status text (Service Unavailable).

warmup.description: List of upstream URLs to pre-establish HTTP/2 sessions at bundle startup. Reduces latency on the first real request.

requireForwardedHeaders.description: Opt-in deterministic proxied-request classification. When true, a request is classified as proxied ONLY when it carries an X-Forwarded-Host header — the port-less-Host heuristic is disabled, so internal calls addressed by service/DNS name (container health probes on app routes, mesh hops, sibling-bundle requests) can no longer rewrite the worker's reverse-proxy host context. Enable only behind a front proxy that always sends X-Forwarded-Host. Defaults to false (historical heuristic: port-less Host OR X-Forwarded-Host).

releaseWatch.description: Stale built-release watch for LOCAL production rehearsals — hard-gated on scope `local` + a non-dev env, never active on a real cluster. When enabled, the bundle watches its SOURCE tree, compares fingerprints against the manifest release stamp, surfaces staleness on GET /_gina/release/status (+ the /_gina/release/events SSE stream) and rebuilds via POST /_gina/release/rebuild with an idle-gated restart (in-flight requests + gina.registerBusyProbe application probes). Fail-closed: disabled by default.

mode.description: notify (default): surface staleness and wait for the operator. auto: rebuild on change automatically — the restart stays idle-gated.

debounceMs.description: Watch-event batch debounce window in ms. Defaults to 750.

reconcileIntervalMs.description: Optional slow re-fingerprint sweep interval in ms for event-lossy mounts; 0 (the default) disables the sweep.

restartMode.description: How a rebuild restarts the process. daemon (default): drain, then spawn `gina bundle:restart` (needs the framework daemon). supervisor: drain, then exit(0) for a container/orchestrator to respawn — the daemonless `gina-container` launch path; requires a restart-on-clean-exit policy (a k8s Deployment or `docker run --restart=always` qualifies; `--restart=on-failure` does not).

cache.description: Bundle-wide render/output-cache defaults. `type` / `store` here are folded into the runtime `server.cache` (which also carries the per-env `enable` / `path` / `ttl` / `maxEntries` from env.json), so they act as the default a route inherits when its own `cache` omits them.

type.description: Bundle-wide default cache strategy. A per-route `cache.type` overrides it; a route with `cache` set but no `type` inherits it. `memory` = in-process (volatile); `fs` = disk-backed (restart-surviving); `redis` = shared L2 across replicas + per-replica L1.

store.description: Required for `redis`: the name of a `connectors.json` entry ({ "<name>": { "connector": "redis", "host": …, "port": … } }) providing the L2 connection. Ignored for memory / fs.

name.description: Optional RFC 9211 Cache-Status identifier for this bundle's render/output cache (default `gina-cache`). Grammar is a conservative RFC 8941 token subset: a letter, then up to 63 of [A-Za-z0-9._-]. An invalid value is ignored with a boot warn. When `server.hidePoweredBy` is true and the cache is enabled, leaving it unset logs a boot warn naming the disclosure — set any token (e.g. `cache`) to close it, or explicitly `gina-cache` to keep the default wire and silence the warn.

session.description: Session plugin defaults (#CSRF1, #COMPLY4) — cookie flags and the absolute-timeout cap the gina.plugins.Session() wrapper applies at factory-call time. Options set explicitly in bundle code always win. Boot config: changes need a bundle restart. The session-record TTL is NOT set here — it comes from the store's connectors.json entry or constructor options, and follows the cookie maxAge when neither is set.

absoluteTimeout.description: Absolute session cap in MILLISECONDS, measured from login (the anchor req.login() stamps at session-id rotation; manually-bound sessions are anchored one request later). Opt-in: when set, an authenticated session older than this is destroyed on its next request — regardless of activity — and the request proceeds with a fresh anonymous session. Bundle code passing session({ absoluteTimeout }) wins over this default; absoluteTimeout: false in bundle code disables it. Composes with idle expiry: the cookie maxAge and the store-record TTL roll with activity, this cap does not.

cookie.description: Defaults for the express-session cookie object. Only these three flags are read from settings; every other cookie option (maxAge, path, domain, ...) is passed in bundle code.

sameSite.description: SameSite default. Matched case-insensitively at runtime; use the lowercase canonical form. "none" requires secure=true (browser-parity invariant, refused at factory call time otherwise).

httpOnly.description: HttpOnly default — keeps the session cookie out of document.cookie.

secure.description: Secure default: true, false, or "auto" (express-session derives the flag from the connection scheme). SameSite=None with secure not strictly true refuses at factory call time.

integrationMode.description: How Socket.io attaches to the HTTP server.

pingTimeout.description: Time to wait for a pong before considering the connection dropped (e.g. "10s", "20s").

maxFieldsSize.description: Maximum total size of multipart form fields (e.g. "8MB", "50MB").

response.description: HTTP response header overrides, typically used for CORS.

header.description: Static response headers added to every response from this bundle.

swig.description: Opt-in override for the swig template engine. When useProject is true the bundle loads the project-pinned package from the project's node_modules instead of the framework's bundled copy — provided the project version satisfies the framework's same-major and minimum-version constraint. A rejected override falls back to the framework copy and logs a warning at bundle startup.

useProject.description: When true, attempt to load the package from <projectPath>/node_modules. When false or omitted, always load the framework's bundled copy (default, current behaviour).

package.description: npm package name to resolve. Defaults to @rhinostone/swig (native swig syntax). Set to @rhinostone/swig-twig to use the Twig-syntax frontend. The abandoned upstream "swig" name is never accepted.

autoescape.description: Whether swig auto-escapes variable output (`{{ x }}`) by default, passed to swig.setDefaults({ autoescape }). Defaults to false today; set true to HTML-escape variable output as an XSS defense — nunjucks defaults to true (see settings.nunjucks.autoescape).

template.description: Per-engine custom template loader (async loader extension point). When a loader is configured the engine resolves templates through it instead of the local filesystem, enabling remote / CDN / object-storage / in-memory template backends. Bundles without a loader render from disk exactly as before.

loader.description: Custom async loader for the swig render path. Mirrors the connectors.json convention: a named built-in `type` plus type-specific flat keys. When present, the bundle renders via the isolated per-bundle swig engine (controller.render-swig-async.js) instead of the filesystem path.

type.description: Built-in loader name. "memory" loads templates from an inline `templates` map (no network or filesystem). "http" fetches templates over HTTP(S) from a configured origin + basePath, with a TTL'd source cache and opt-in ETag revalidation.

templates.description: For type "memory": flat map of template identifier to source string.

origin.description: For type "http": scheme://host[:port] of the template origin (no path). http or https. Required for the http loader.

basePath.description: For type "http": path prefix under origin that template identifiers resolve against (root-relative, flat namespace). Defaults to "". Resolved URLs are containment-checked to stay under origin+basePath.

ttl.description: For type "http": source-cache TTL in seconds (absolute from fetch). Defaults to 60. Raise it for immutable CDN-published templates; 0 caches until evicted.

revalidate.description: For type "http": when true, a cache hit issues a conditional GET (If-None-Match) and serves cached source on 304, refreshing the TTL. Off by default (no per-hit round-trip). Turn on for live-CMS templates whose origin emits ETags.

cache.description: #TPL1 Tier-2 opt-in: reuse compiled templates across requests via the shared per-bundle engine + AsyncLocalStorage per-request context. Off by default (per-request render, no compiled-template reuse). Force-disabled in dev mode regardless so template edits are picked up live without a restart.

loader.description: Custom async loader for the nunjucks render path. Mirrors the connectors.json convention: a named built-in `type` plus type-specific flat keys. When present, the bundle renders via a per-request nunjucks Environment over this loader (controller.render-nunjucks-async.js) instead of the cached-Environment filesystem path.

type.description: Built-in loader name. "memory" loads templates from an inline `templates` map (no network or filesystem). "http" fetches templates over HTTP(S) from a configured origin + basePath, with a TTL'd source cache and opt-in ETag revalidation.

templates.description: For type "memory": flat map of template identifier to source string.

origin.description: For type "http": scheme://host[:port] of the template origin (no path). http or https. Required for the http loader.

basePath.description: For type "http": path prefix under origin that template identifiers resolve against (root-relative, flat namespace). Defaults to "". Resolved URLs are containment-checked to stay under origin+basePath.

ttl.description: For type "http": source-cache TTL in seconds (absolute from fetch). Defaults to 60. Raise it for immutable CDN-published templates; 0 caches until evicted.

revalidate.description: For type "http": when true, a cache hit issues a conditional GET (If-None-Match) and serves cached source on 304, refreshing the TTL. Off by default (no per-hit round-trip). Turn on for live-CMS templates whose origin emits ETags.

cache.description: #TPL1 Tier-2 opt-in: reuse compiled templates across requests via a shared per-request-context (AsyncLocalStorage) nunjucks Environment. Off by default (per-request Environment, no compiled-template reuse). Force-disabled in dev mode regardless so template edits are picked up live without a restart.

render.description: Template engine dispatch. Selects which delegate file (controller.render-swig.js or controller.render-nunjucks.js) handles self.render() calls for this bundle. Switching to "nunjucks" requires `npm install nunjucks` in the project root — the framework does not bundle nunjucks.

engine.description: Bundle-level template engine for self.render() HTML output. "swig" (default) uses @rhinostone/swig via controller.render-swig.js; "nunjucks" uses the project-installed nunjucks package via controller.render-nunjucks.js. When set to "nunjucks", bundle startup fails with NUNJUCKS_NOT_INSTALLED if the package is absent from the project's node_modules. An explicit template extension overrides this per render: a section whose templates.json `ext` is ".njk" (or a self.setTemplate(file, '.njk') call) renders through nunjucks, ".swig" through swig — so a single bundle can mix engines; ".html" and any other extension follow this setting.

nunjucks.description: Configuration for the nunjucks template engine (when render.engine is "nunjucks"). The package is never framework-bundled — it must exist in the project's node_modules.

package.description: npm package name to resolve in <projectPath>/node_modules. Defaults to "nunjucks" (upstream).

autoescape.description: Whether the nunjucks Environment autoescapes by default. Passed to `new nunjucks.Environment(loader, { autoescape })`.
